points.title: 贵族出身
points.description: 凯撒出生于罗马一个古老但已衰落的贵族家庭，属于尤利乌斯氏族。他的父亲同名，曾担任过罗马的行政长官。尽管家族显赫，但在凯撒出生时，家道已经中落。凯撒的童年正值罗马共和国末期，政治动荡，社会矛盾尖锐。他接受了良好的教育，学习修辞学、哲学和法律，展现出非凡的才华和雄心。这段时期奠定了他对罗马政治体系的深刻理解，也培养了他日后政治斗争所需的口才和智慧。
points.descriptionEn: Caesar was born into an ancient but declining noble family, the Julian clan. His father, also named Gaius Julius Caesar, had served as a praetor. Although the family was prestigious, they had fallen on hard times by Caesar's birth. Caesar's childhood coincided with the late Roman Republic, a period of political turmoil and social conflict. He received an excellent education in rhetoric, philosophy, and law, displaying exceptional talent and ambition. This period laid his deep understanding of the Roman political system and cultivated the oratory skills and wisdom needed for his future political struggles.

points.title: 军旅生涯开始
points.description: 凯撒的父亲去世后，他按照罗马传统进入军旅生涯，在东方服役。在服役期间，他展现了非凡的军事才能，曾因救援一位罗马公民而获得花冠奖励。他还曾被海盗俘虏，但表现出非凡的镇定和勇气，甚至反过来威胁海盗会处死他们。获释后，他果然组织力量追捕并处死了这些海盗。这段经历锻炼了凯撒的军事才能和领导能力，也塑造了他无所畏惧的性格。同时，他与当时罗马的军事统帅苏拉产生了政治对立，被迫离开罗马前往东方。
points.descriptionEn: After his father's death, Caesar began his military career according to Roman tradition, serving in the East. During his service, he demonstrated exceptional military talent, once receiving a civic crown for rescuing a Roman citizen. He was also captured by pirates but showed remarkable composure and courage, even threatening to have them executed. After his release, he organized forces to capture and execute the pirates. This experience honed Caesar's military skills and leadership abilities, shaping his fearless character. Simultaneously, he developed political opposition to the Roman military general Sulla, forcing him to leave Rome for the East.

points.title: 政治崛起
points.description: 苏拉去世后，凯撒返回罗马，开始积极投身政治。他通过联姻和结盟，逐渐在罗马政坛崭露头角。凯撒担任过财务官、市政官和大祭司等职务，积累了丰富的政治经验。他通过慷慨的公共支出和精彩的演说赢得了平民的支持，同时也与庞培和克拉苏形成了政治同盟，史称'前三头同盟'。凯撒还通过举办盛大的公共活动和游戏，提高了自己的声望。这一时期，凯撒展现了卓越的政治手腕和野心，为日后的崛起奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: After Sulla's death, Caesar returned to Rome and actively engaged in politics. Through marriages and alliances, he gradually emerged in Roman politics. Caesar held positions such as quaestor, aedile, and pontifex maximus, accumulating rich political experience. He won the support of the common people through generous public expenditures and brilliant speeches, while forming a political alliance with Pompey and Crassus, known as the 'First Triumvirate.' Caesar also enhanced his reputation by hosting grand public events and games. During this period, Caesar demonstrated exceptional political skill and ambition, laying the foundation for his future rise.

points.title: 高卢征服
points.description: 凯撒被任命为高卢总督，开始了为期八年的高卢征服战争。在这期间，他率领罗马军团征服了整个高卢地区（大致相当于今天的法国、比利时等地），击败了各部落的抵抗。凯撒详细记录了这些战役，著有《高卢战记》，成为研究古代军事的重要文献。高卢战争不仅为罗马带来了巨大的财富和奴隶，也极大地增强了凯撒的军事威望和私人财富。他建立了忠诚的军队，积累了足够的政治资本，为他日后返回罗马挑战元老院权威奠定了基础。这段经历是凯撒一生中最辉煌的军事成就。
points.descriptionEn: Caesar was appointed governor of Gaul and began an eight-year conquest of Gaul. During this period, he led Roman legions to conquer the entire region of Gaul (roughly corresponding to modern-day France, Belgium, etc.), defeating the resistance of various tribes. Caesar meticulously documented these campaigns in his 'Commentaries on the Gallic War,' which became an important source for studying ancient military history. The Gallic War brought enormous wealth and slaves to Rome, significantly enhancing Caesar's military prestige and personal fortune. He built a loyal army and accumulated sufficient political capital, laying the foundation for his future challenge to the Senate's authority upon returning to Rome. This period represents Caesar's most brilliant military achievement.

points.title: 内战与独裁
points.description: 凯撒与元老院的矛盾激化，元老院命令他解除兵权返回罗马。凯撒拒绝服从，于公元前49年率军渡过卢比孔河，发动内战，击败了庞培和元老院势力。随后，他成为罗马的独裁官，进行了一系列改革，包括改革历法（创立儒略历）、改革土地制度、扩大公民权等。凯撒还重建了卡皮托利诺山上的朱庇特神庙，并在罗马建造了许多公共建筑。他的独裁统治虽然结束了罗马共和国的内战，但也为罗马从共和国向帝国的转变铺平了道路。这一时期，凯撒的权力达到顶峰，但也埋下了被刺杀的种子。
points.descriptionEn: The conflict between Caesar and the Senate intensified when the Senate ordered him to relinquish his command and return to Rome. Caesar refused to comply and in 49 BC, he led his army across the Rubicon River, triggering a civil war in which he defeated Pompey and the Senate's forces. Subsequently, he became dictator of Rome and implemented a series of reforms, including reforming the calendar (creating the Julian calendar), land reform, and expanding citizenship rights. Caesar also rebuilt the Temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill and constructed many public buildings in Rome. His dictatorship ended Rome's civil wars but paved the way for the transition from Republic to Empire. During this period, Caesar's power reached its zenith, but it also sowed the seeds of his assassination.

points.title: 遇刺身亡
points.description: 凯撒被授予终身独裁官和'祖国之父'等荣誉，权力日益集中，引起共和派贵族的恐惧和不满。公元前44年3月15日，凯撒在元老院被一群共和派贵族刺杀，其中包括布鲁图斯和卡西乌斯等曾经是他盟友的人。刺杀者声称是为了恢复共和制，但凯撒的死亡反而导致了罗马更大规模的内战，最终由他的养子屋大维（后来的奥古斯都）建立罗马帝国。凯撒的遇刺成为西方历史上最著名的政治暗杀之一，也标志着罗马共和国的终结和罗马帝国的开始。
points.descriptionEn: Caesar was granted honors such as dictator for life and 'Father of the Fatherland,' with increasingly concentrated power, which aroused fear and dissatisfaction among republican aristocrats. On March 15, 44 BC, Caesar was assassinated in the Senate by a group of republican nobles, including Brutus and Cassius, who had once been his allies. The assassins claimed to act to restore the Republic, but Caesar's death instead led to larger-scale civil wars in Rome, ultimately resulting in the establishment of the Roman Empire by his adopted son Octavian (later Augustus). Caesar's assassination became one of the most famous political assassinations in Western history, marking the end of the Roman Republic and the beginning of the Roman Empire.

appraisal.zh: 凯撒通常被视为罗马最伟大的军事家与政治家之一，他终结了长达一个世纪的内战，历法、土地与公民权改革为罗马社会奠定基础，军事征服既拓展疆域也带来财富与文化交流。但另一种看法认为他是共和国的破坏者：以军事力量与政治手腕攫取权力，开专制先例，征服高卢造成大量死亡，个人野心最终招致遇刺与更多动荡。学界因此将他定义为改革者与独裁者的矛盾复合体，其名也成为个人权力与共和传统冲突的象征。
appraisal.en: Caesar is generally seen as one of Rome's greatest commanders and statesmen: he ended a century of civil war, his calendar, land and citizenship reforms laid foundations for Roman society, and his conquests expanded the empire while bringing wealth and cultural exchange. Another view holds him a destroyer of the Republic, seizing power through military force and political maneuvering, setting a precedent for autocracy, causing mass Gallic deaths, and letting personal ambition provoke his assassination and further turmoil. Scholarship thus defines him as a contradictory blend of reformer and dictator, his name a symbol of the conflict between personal power and republican tradition.

supporter.zh: 凯撒被视为罗马历史上最伟大的军事家和政治家之一。他结束了罗马长达一个世纪的内战，为罗马带来了和平与繁荣。他的改革措施，包括历法改革、土地改革和扩大公民权，为罗马社会的发展奠定了基础。凯撒的领导才能和远见卓识使他能够应对复杂的政治局势，为罗马从共和国向帝国的平稳过渡做出了重要贡献。他的军事征服不仅扩大了罗马的疆域，也为罗马带来了巨大的财富和文化交流。
supporter.en: Caesar is regarded as one of the greatest military commanders and statesmen in Roman history. He ended Rome's century-long civil wars, bringing peace and prosperity to the empire. His reform measures, including calendar reform, land reform, and expanded citizenship rights, laid the foundation for Roman social development. Caesar's leadership and vision enabled him to navigate complex political situations, making significant contributions to the smooth transition from Republic to Empire. His military conquests not only expanded Rome's territories but also brought immense wealth and cultural exchange to the Roman world.

critic.zh: 批评者认为凯撒是独裁者和共和国的破坏者。他通过军事力量和政治手腕攫取权力，破坏了罗马共和国的传统政治制度。凯撒的独裁统治虽然结束了内战，但也为后来的专制统治开了先例。他的征服战争导致大量高卢人死亡，给被征服地区带来了灾难。此外，凯撒的个人野心和权力欲望最终导致了他的遇刺，引发了更多的内战和动荡。批评者认为，凯撒的统治方式违背了共和制的精神，是罗马政治衰落的开始。
critic.en: Critics view Caesar as a dictator and destroyer of the Republic. He seized power through military force and political maneuvering, undermining Rome's traditional political institutions. Although Caesar's dictatorship ended the civil wars, it set a precedent for later autocratic rule. His conquest wars resulted in numerous Gallic deaths and brought disaster to conquered regions. Furthermore, Caesar's personal ambition and lust for power ultimately led to his assassination, triggering more civil wars and turmoil. Critics argue that Caesar's methods of governance violated the spirit of the Republic and marked the beginning of Rome's political decline.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，凯撒被复杂地定义为一个既是改革者又是独裁者的矛盾人物。他既是罗马共和国的终结者，也是罗马帝国制度的奠基人。凯撒的形象在历史文献中既有正面记载也有负面评价，反映了罗马社会对他的复杂态度。在流行文化中，凯撒常被塑造为权力与野心的象征，莎士比亚的《尤利乌斯·凯撒》戏剧使他的形象广为人知。凯撒的生平和事迹成为西方政治文化的重要象征，他的名字成为'凯撒主义'的代名词，代表着个人独裁与共和传统的永恒冲突。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Caesar is complexly defined as a contradictory figure who was both a reformer and a dictator. He was both the terminator of the Roman Republic and the founder of the Roman imperial system. Caesar's image in historical sources contains both positive and negative accounts, reflecting the complex attitudes of Roman society toward him. In popular culture, Caesar is often portrayed as a symbol of power and ambition, with Shakespeare's play 'Julius Caesar' making his image widely known. Caesar's life and deeds have become important symbols in Western political culture, and his name has become synonymous with 'Caesarism,' representing the eternal conflict between personal autocracy and republican tradition.
